### [non-spec.18.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: CODE-3 moves the OnClaimed hook to the claim boundary (after the claim and any slot reservation, before resolveSandbox/DialAdapter/NegotiateVersion) by splitting `connect` into a claim half and a handshake half; item 3's release trigger widens to "a hook error, or a resolve, dial, or handshake failure after the hook" with the same per-path helpers, and the cl.Close steps go — BECAUSE SPEC-1b item 2 ("before the first RPC to the pod") is the home and needs no edit; a post-hook handshake failure then spends a retry through item 3.7, bounding pod loss by maxRetries — ALTERNATIVES: reword SPEC-1b to "first entry-touching RPC" and only release the claim on connect failure (spec loop closed; a handshake failure would stay "pre-claim", spending no retry, so a broken-adapter pool drains one pod per backoff for the whole window); hook inside the claim half before reserveResumeSlot (a concurrent start can reserve a sibling slot between claim CREATE and reservation, so the hook-error DeleteClaim would evict siblings — the round-1 defect).
DECISION: the handshake-failure release in `Claim` is unconditional, so create (nil hook) also deletes the claim on a failed handshake — BECAUSE conditioning on a non-nil hook is a branch with no spec basis, and DeleteClaim is the gateway's drain (reclaim.go `drain`), so the broken pod is not returned to idle.
FACT: `connect` (claimconnect.go) has two callers, `Claim` (bindclaim.go, which `Bind` and create use) and `Binder.Resume`; `connectSlot` has two, `BindSlot` and the slot claim at slotbinder.go:163. A connect handshake failure today closes the client and deletes no claim on either exclusive path; connectSlot's handshake failures are SlotBindErrors the slot retry policy releases. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/claimconnect.go:60-112, slotbinder.go:635-694
FACT: DeleteClaim is the gateway's reclaim (drain) action; the WPC projects the occupancy phase on the claim DELETE. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/reclaim.go:87-100
WATCHOUT: `reserveResumeSlot` takes `sb.Name` today; after the split it takes the claimed sandbox name before `resolveSandbox`. `Claim`'s PodClaim phase timing will include the hook's store write on Bind. EVIDENCE: resume.go:129-145, bindclaim.go:56-74
OPEN: a `reserveResumeSlot` failure on Resume is after the claim and before the hook, so CODE-4 item 3.5 calls it pre-claim and nothing releases the claim (pre-existing; not this finding). A later round should decide whether it is a separate finding.

### [spec.1.review-performance.1]
DECISION: Returned no findings in redesign-4 spec round 1. BECAUSE the redesign-4 additions (SPEC-1g credential assignment on the restore, the Retry accounting widening, SPEC-1e item 5, SPEC-2c item 8, SPEC-3q, SPEC-5d2, the podless-miss `resume_pending` in the path 6 lead, the pre-running delivery point, and SPEC-5z item 10) add no etcd write and no new watch. The only new per-unit store work is one Token Service assignment per resume and one DLQ peek per commit to `running` from a pre-running state (at most 200/s at Tier 3). Neither approaches a stated budget. — ALTERNATIVES: (1) Warm-pool claim demand from idle-suspension resumes. Rejected: spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1040 "Expected claim rate" is generic and operator-measured, and the bound depends on the workload. (2) etcd claim churn per suspend/resume cycle. Rejected: the bound is about 10,000/900 s ≈ 11 extra claims/s × about 5 writes, roughly 60 writes/s, against the ~800/s Tier 3 estimate (spec/04_system-components.md:473). (3) Token Service outage blocking the resume of idle-released sessions. Rejected: the proposal's Edge cases accept it explicitly ("Pre-claim failure"), and it follows from the owner's option A.
FACT: Credential leases end to end. Idle suspension (hold zero) releases the pod, and §7.1 step 23 returns lease L1. The driver runs the pre-claim availability check (spec/04_system-components.md:1326), claims P2, writes `resuming` (generation incremented), handshakes, and calls AssignCredentials (L2) → Resume (spec/04_system-components.md:864). At AssignCredentials, L2 is recorded against P2's SPIFFE URI (spec/04_system-components.md:1624), so the resumed runtime can reach its provider through the proxy. EVIDENCE: as cited.
WATCHOUT: A driver attempt whose replica crashes after AssignCredentials and before the commit leaks its leases until lease TTL (default 3600 s, spec/04_system-components.md:1257 table). Those leases count against the credential's `maxConcurrentSessions`. The create path has the same leak. Do not file it as a 0092 regression unless the leak reaches a stated budget. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md SPEC-1g last sentence.

### [spec.1.review-reliability.1]
DECISION: returned no findings in redesign-4 spec round 1 — BECAUSE tracing credential leases (running → idle-suspended hold zero → checkpoint, conditional binding clear, release returning L1 per §7.1 step 23 → message → DLQ enqueue → suspended → resume_pending → driver pre-claim check → claim P2 → resuming write (generation +1) → AssignCredentials L2 recorded against P2's SPIFFE URI → Resume → commit → held delivery) found no loss, double-apply, or stall that is new, unaccepted, and fixable in the staged spec. Crash leaks (an attempt's leases after AssignCredentials, a stopped attempt's pod) are bounded by lease TTL and the claim-orphan GC respectively — ALTERNATIVES: filing the crashed-attempt lease leak (rejected: TTL-bounded, same as the create path; see spec.1.review-performance WATCHOUT); filing the failed-re-read answer in **Enqueue racing a terminal transition.** as a duplicate source (rejected: a removal that finds the entry still does not prove non-delivery, so no spec wording closes it, and it needs a Postgres failure on one replica only).
FACT: The resume window (§7.3 step 3c), the resuming watchdog (300 s, §6.2), the suspended lifetime, and the interrupt hold are all anchored on row fields, so each survives a coordinator restart; the driver's pre-claim backoff is jittered in CODE-4 item 1.5 and flag item 12. EVIDENCE: spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:241; non-spec-changes.md:81, :125
DEFERRED [non-spec-changes.md]: CODE-6 item 5.2/5.3 `TurnInFlight` reads only the local executor's `sending` counter and turn token, so after a coordinator handoff (a rolling update included) the adopter reports no turn in flight while the runtime may still be processing a message the previous coordinator delivered; `SuspendIdle` can then suspend and checkpoint a session mid-turn when no qualifying event arrived for `maxClientIdleSeconds`. The spec predicate (SPEC-5f "no message delivered to it is still being processed") is correct and implementable from the adapter's `ready_for_input` (spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:327, :329); the code approximation is what is wrong after handoff. A non-spec reviewer should decide whether this meets the bar. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md:187-188
WATCHOUT: SPEC-1b's "No session's `pod_assignment` names that pod, so ... drains it" assumes no sibling joined the attempt's freshly claimed concurrent pod; the archive records that a concurrent start can reserve a sibling slot on it (review-log-archive.md:1375), and then the GC predicate (spec/04_system-components.md:517 "whose pod no active session references") never fires for the stopped attempt's slot. spec.1.review-kubernetes said not to refile and the archive (review-log-archive.md:2414) judged the slot leak pre-existing on every release path; I did not file it. Refile only with a concrete reclaimer that the spec should name.

USEFUL [Standing context "Refuted: store-outage degradation" and "Refuted: GC races"]: covered the DLQ-on-Redis-loss and binding-clear-before-release candidates again.

### [spec.1.review-security.1]

FACT: Credential leases traced end to end for running → idle-suspended → released → message-resumed. The release revokes the pod's leases (SPEC-5b, SPEC-1g citing §7.1 step 23); the driver runs the §4.9 pre-claim check before the claim, then assigns new leases after the entry write and before `Resume` (SPEC-1g, SPEC-3q). §4.9 records the issuing pod's SPIFFE URI at `AssignCredentials` time, so the new leases bind to the replacement pod and no lease stays bound to the released pod. The multi-tenant deliveryMode/isolation admission check is stated for "every path that mints a credential lease", so it covers the restore without a staged edit. EVIDENCE: spec/04_system-components.md:1623-1628, :864, :1324-1326; spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:26.
FACT: The Standard/Basic credential-rotation restart (§4.7.8, §4.9 Fallback Flow step 7) is not modelled in the session state machine and has no implementation in pkg/gateway, so it does not conflict with SPEC-1b "no other component writes resume_pending → resuming". EVIDENCE: spec/04_system-components.md:1517, :864.
WATCHOUT: SPEC-1g says "one lease per provider the resolution names", while §4.9 **Intersection at session creation.** skips providers that have no available credential at creation. Whether a partial assignment on resume fails the attempt is unstated. This is availability semantics rather than security, so it is not filed under this lens. EVIDENCE: spec/04_system-components.md:1434.
WATCHOUT: The Redis DLQ and inbox keys are not in the §12.8 DeleteByUser order (12_storage-architecture.md:840-852). With the durable-inbox EXPIRE deleted (OD-R2, owner-settled), the inbox key of an erased user's session has no expiry. It is recorded as RECORDS-1 7(k) with the default applied. Do not refile it as a spec finding unless the owner reopens OD-R2.

### [spec.2.review-mechanism.1]
FACT: The credential trace holds end to end in the staged spec. Idle suspension releases the pod, and SPEC-1g says the release returns the session's leases (§7.1 step 23). The driver resolves pools and runs the pre-claim check before the claim, so a failure there writes nothing (item 1). AssignCredentials runs after the resuming write and before Resume, and it mints leases whose SPIFFE binding is the replacement pod's (§4.9 SPIFFE-binding item 1 records the issuing pod at AssignCredentials time). Any failure after the claim is reported as runtime_crash and classified at §7.3 step 2 (SPEC-1b item 3). EVIDENCE: spec/04_system-components.md:1624, spec-changes.md:69, :153
FACT: When a §10.1.2 step 1 CAS fails because a resume-driver bump landed between step 0 and step 1, the adopter discards its lease claim and restarts from lease acquisition (§10.1.2 step 1). The existing 0-row path covers this, and on the restart step 0 finds `resuming`, which SPEC-2a does not adopt. EVIDENCE: spec/10_gateway-internals.md:37
WATCHOUT: The checkpoint-manifest resume selection filters on MAX(coordination_generation). Resume-driver bumps keep that selection correct because the bumps are monotonic, so do not file it as broken by the driver's increment. EVIDENCE: spec/10_gateway-internals.md:171
WATCHOUT: §6.2 line 176 ("policy rejections are not retried") concerns the running-session pod-crash path. SPEC-1c removing "policy rejection" from the `resuming` non-retryable example does not contradict it. EVIDENCE: spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:176, :242

### [spec.3.review-performance.1]
DECISION: Returned no findings in redesign-4 spec round 3. BECAUSE the r1-to-r3 diff (SPEC-1b item 3 failure-reason classification, the SPEC-1c bullet relabel and example swap, SPEC-1e item 6, SPEC-1g2) adds no store write, watch, or per-unit work. It only reclassifies post-claim failures, and the retry budget bounds each of them. ALTERNATIVES: (1) A Token Service outage after the claim spends a retry and a warm pod for each attempt. Rejected: pool lease minting goes through the gateway's in-process `Credentials.AssignProto` (pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/credentiallease.go:99), and the real keys sit in the gateway's Token Service cache (spec/04_system-components.md:1588). So it is speculative that an outage reaches the post-claim mint at all. (2) A credential exhaustion between the pre-claim check and the assignment spends a retry. Rejected: the window is only the claim plus the handshake, so the event is rare and bounded by maxRetries. (3) A corrupt checkpoint is now reported as `runtime_crash` and retried, which costs up to maxRetries+1 checkpoint downloads. Rejected: the cost is bounded by a small constant factor.
FACT: `assignCredentials` fails the whole attempt when any one provider's `AssignProto` fails (credentiallease.go:98-106), while §4.9 "Intersection at session creation" says providers without an available credential are skipped (spec/04_system-components.md:1434). This mismatch predates 0092 and also affects finalize. SPEC-1g's "one lease per provider the resolution names" follows the code. Do not file it against 0092. EVIDENCE: as cited.
FACT: The §4.9 pre-claim check reads pool utilization, cooldown, and health only. It does not consult the §4.3 Token Service circuit breaker. EVIDENCE: spec/04_system-components.md:1326, :222-228.

### [spec.5.review-mechanism.1]
FACT: Under SPEC-1g the restore's Token Service call is `AssignCredentials`, which runs after the `resume_pending → resuming` write. A Token Service outage is therefore a post-claim failure that spends a retry under SPEC-1b **Retry accounting.**, and it is not a pre-claim failure. The pre-claim availability check reads pool utilization, cooldown, and health, and it does not call the Token Service. EVIDENCE: spec/04_system-components.md:1326 (pre-claim check), :1554 ("the replacement pod also requires `AssignCredentials` (which calls the Token Service)"); spec-changes.md:155; non-spec-changes.md:48 (hook precedes `AssignCredentials`).

FACT: The credential lease path traces cleanly for running → idle-suspended → released → resumed. The release returns the leases (SPEC-1g citing §7.1 step 23). The driver runs the pre-claim check before the claim. `AssignCredentials` runs after the entry write and before `Resume`, and it records the new pod's SPIFFE URI (spec/04_system-components.md:1624). The credential file is written before `session_start` (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:26). §4.7.1 admits `AssignCredentials` then `Resume` under one token (rule 4 creates the entry and `Resume` resolves it). No other finding.
UNVERIFIED: The 300 s `resuming` watchdog (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:241, "matching the setup-command total timeout") also bounds a snapshotless rebuild, which runs materialization plus setup inside `resuming`. `setupPolicy.timeoutSeconds` is per runtime and can be set above 300 s (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:204). A long setup may therefore never rebuild. This was not filed because resume-time setup predates 0092 (§15.1 SETUP_COMMAND_FAILED "resume-time setup"). A non-spec or human reviewer should decide whether it matters.

### [spec.1.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: the suspension release moves the session inbox to the DLQ after the guarded `PodAssignment` clear and before the pod release (SPEC-5b step 2 cites the §7.2 inbox-to-DLQ migration; CODE-6 item 4 step 3 calls `migrateInboxOnResumePending`) — BECAUSE a podless suspended session holds no lease, so the old holder's in-memory inbox was otherwise stranded and escaped the terminal DLQ drain — ALTERNATIVES: keep the lease while the inbox is non-empty (reintroduces podless lease-holding), restore a SPEC-5c drain on the podless `resume_pending` write (drains only the writer's own empty inbox), accept the loss (breaks the §7.2 alive-coordinator guarantee).
WATCHOUT: the migration must follow the clear. Before the clear, a held-pod resume's `deliverBuffered` can be mid-`Send` on an inbox entry the drain moves to the DLQ, duplicating delivery; after the clear the step-3 guard and the `resumeHeldPod` guard exclude it, so no delivery lock is needed. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 4 step 3 and tail sentence "The release takes no delivery lock."
FACT: migrated entries are scored at acceptance time (SPEC-5z item 7), so they predate `SuspendedAt` and the interrupt **Backlog resume.** check (DLQ entries accepted after `SuspendedAt`) does not count them; an `Idle` release counts them in the DLQ. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 2 **`HeldLen`.**
FACT: `migrateInboxOnResumePending` is the only wrapper of `MigrateInboxToDLQ` in the session server and its only production caller was failure.go:360; its doc comment still says "EXPIRE" for durable mode, which CODE-4 item 18 removes. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/messaging.go:102-118

### [spec.1.fix-G2.1]
DECISION: A failed admission write (any StampSync error other than ErrSessionSuspended) fails open: the message is delivered unrecorded. SPEC-5f **Idle suspension.** states it in one sentence citing §12.3; CODE-6 item 5.5 puts the policy in StampSync (log, no lastWrite, return nil) — BECAUSE §12.3 **Behavior during Postgres failover:** and §10.1.3 say existing sessions continue, and the shipped async Stamp drops store failures — ALTERNATIVES: fail closed with staged §12.3/§10.1.3 exceptions (stops delivery to every running session for up to 30 s); hold in the DLQ (client gets `queued`, delivered up to 15 min later); classify the error in PodExecutor.Send item 5.2 (puts suspension policy in the executor, changes 5.2 and its test).
WATCHOUT: Fail-open leaves a residual window: while the store is unreachable no `running → suspended` write can land either, but a SuspendIdle that read a stale replica row and lands its write just as the primary returns could suspend over an unrecorded delivery. Do not add a per-replica "unrecorded delivery" marker to close it; the check and write cannot be atomic without the store. — EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md SPEC-5f **Idle suspension.**; pgstore Get reads the replica while Update goes to the primary.
WATCHOUT: StampSync has no timeout of its own; a hung primary stalls Send until the caller's context ends. A timeout knob was deliberately not added in this round; file it separately if needed. — EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 5.1

The old CODE-6 item 5.5 justification ("a delivery already depends on the store") was also false for a running session's message path.
FACT: The shipped Stamper.Stamp runs `go s.persist(...)` off the request path and drops failures. — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/session/sessionidle/sessionidle.go (Stamp, persist)

### [spec.1.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: The release migrates the in-memory inbox to the DLQ right after the guarded clear of `PodAssignment` and before the pod release (SPEC-5b step 2 by citing the §7.2 inbox-to-DLQ migration paragraph; CODE-6 item 4 step 3 calls `migrateInboxOnResumePending`). It takes no delivery lock. BECAUSE the clear's guard and the `resumeHeldPod` guard already exclude a held-pod resume after the clear, so no `deliverBuffered` on this replica can be reading the inbox (the next one needs a driver claim and restore). The migrated entries keep their acceptance scores (SPEC-5z item 7), so they are older than `SuspendedAt`, the interrupt backlog check does not count them, and the next resume or the terminal DLQ drain handles them. ALTERNATIVES: migrate before the clear. Rejected: a held-pod resume during the checkpoint runs `deliverBuffered` mid-`Send` while the migration drains, which delivers the entry and also leaves it in the DLQ, so it is delivered twice. Closing that would need the delivery lock in the release, and then the Design delivery-lock paragraph, CODE-6 item 4 ("The release takes no delivery lock"), and summary watch-out "covers only the message paths" would all change. Also rejected: keep the lease while the inbox is non-empty, which brings back the podless lease-holding that redesign 5 removed. Also rejected: accept the loss in SPEC-5c, which breaks the §7.2 default-mode guarantee while the replica is alive.
WATCHOUT: This is a migration at the pod release. It is NOT the "inbox-to-DLQ migration on entry to `suspended`" that Standing context Traps forbids. That trap concerns entry. While the pod is held, the coordinator keeps the inbox and `deliverBuffered` reads it. Do not move the migration to the `running → suspended` write. EVIDENCE: review-log.md Standing context "Do not restore".
WATCHOUT: Some windows of a few milliseconds, between the clear and the end of the migration, remain unhandled. In one, a terminate served by another replica runs its terminal drain before the migrated entries land in the DLQ, so those senders get no `target_terminated`. In the other, a crash loses the inbox, which is §7.2's accepted default-mode crash loss. The release adds no re-read for the first case. Refile it only with a path that widens the window.
FACT: `MigrateInboxToDLQ` drains first and then enqueues each entry with `DefaultDLQTTL`, which scores it at `EnqueuedAt` + TTL. `migrateInboxOnResumePending` logs an error and never returns one, so the release continues after a failed migration, as §7.2's failure sentence states for the transition. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/session/sessioninbox/coordinator.go:104-134; pkg/gateway/sessionserver/messaging.go:112-118.

### [spec.1.review-reliability.1]

DECISION: filed one finding. With `durableInbox: false`, the in-memory inbox entries of an interrupt-suspended session are stranded once SPEC-2a drops the lease for a podless row. BECAUSE: path-5 entries buffered before the interrupt stay in the releasing replica's MemoryInbox, the interrupt backlog predicate excludes the inbox, and after the lease lapses any adopter's **Delivery of held messages.** reads only its own inbox. The enterResumePending migration runs on whichever replica writes `resume_pending`. ALTERNATIVES: (1) keep the lease while the inbox is non-empty. Rejected because it brings back a per-row probe. (2) Migrate inbox to DLQ on entry to `suspended`. Rejected because Standing context bars it, since it would let pre-suspension entries undo the interrupt. The suggested remedy is a migration at the SPEC-5b step 2 clear, scored by acceptance time. Those entries predate SuspendedAt, so they do not trigger a resume.
FACT: interrupt does not touch the inbox. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/interrupt.go (no inbox reference). The default-mode guarantee is "does not drop undelivered messages while the coordinating replica remains alive". EVIDENCE: spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:312.
FACT: §6.2 says "The orphan session reconciler skips sessions in `suspended` state with no pod binding." EVIDENCE: spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:236. It is consistent with the podless no-lease rule.
FACT: Every §29.3 route a podless `suspended` session admits has a server after SPEC-2d, SPEC-3j, and SPEC-5l. sweepSuspended does a per-replica listing with an in-memory lifetime compare and no Redis call for podless rows (non-spec CODE-6 item 2.2). The no-per-row-probe constraint holds.
WATCHOUT: the §10.1.5 **Session with no bound pod.** sentence "holds no stream, pending tool call, or buffered event" is false for a replica that holds MemoryInbox entries. If the inbox finding is fixed by migration at release, this sentence becomes true again, so do not edit it separately. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md:143.

### [spec.2.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: the DLQ TTL runs from the later of acceptance and the session's entry to the recovering state it is in (SPEC-5i **Delivery of held messages.** last sentence, its one home); scores stay acceptance + TTL (SPEC-5z item 7) for order; code gate is `sweepDLQExpiry` skipping a row whose `UpdatedAt` is under `DefaultDLQTTL` old (CODE-6 item 12) — BECAUSE entries migrated at the suspension release were accepted before `SuspendedAt`, the interrupt hold (900 s) is at least the TTL (900 s), so an acceptance clock expired every migrated entry at the first `resume_pending` sweep — ALTERNATIVES: reviewer's "most recent entry to `resume_pending`" clock (needs a new column, expires during a slow `resuming`, wrong on the held-pod `suspended → awaiting_client_action` edge); migration-time scores (break acceptance order read by `deliverBuffered` and `CountAcceptedAfter`); deleting the release-time migration (strands the in-memory inbox of a lease-less podless session).
CORRECTS [spec.1.review-mechanism.1]: the FACT that the DLQ-TTL objection to an inbox-to-DLQ move at pod release is "moot after SPEC-5z item 7" is wrong: an acceptance-based clock has already run out when recovery starts. The clock now starts no earlier than entry to the recovering state.

### [spec.2.review-reliability.1]
DECISION: filed one finding. The round-1 release migration (SPEC-5b step 2) moves an interrupt-suspended session's pre-suspension inbox entries into the DLQ, scored at acceptance + maxResumeWindowSeconds (SPEC-5z item 7). The TTL is measured from acceptance and enforced in every recovering state (SPEC-5i **Delivery of held messages.** last sentence), and the hold (900 s) is at least the TTL (900 s). So every migrated entry is already past its TTL at the release, and the 5 s `sweepDLQExpiry` tick in `resume_pending`/`resuming` expires it before the driver's commit delivers it. With the pod still held, the same entries are delivered. BECAUSE: the fix exists to carry these entries to the next resume, and it does not. ALTERNATIVES: score at release time (rejected: it only moves the clock, and a 7-day podless suspension still outlives the TTL); exclude migrated entries from expiry (rejected: it adds a second class of entry).
CORRECTS [spec.1.review-mechanism.1 FACT "The DLQ-TTL scoring objection ... is moot after SPEC-5z item 7 ... and the DLQ TTL being enforced only in recovering states"]: it is not moot. An acceptance-time score makes an entry older than the TTL expire at the first sweep after the session enters `resume_pending`. Recovering-state enforcement only defers the expiry to that moment. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md:525 last sentence; pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/watchdog.go:166 (5 s tick), :684-705.
CORRECTS [spec.1.fix-design-G1.1 DECISION "the next resume or the terminal DLQ drain handles them"]: the next resume expires them with `dlq_ttl_expired` and does not deliver them.
FACT: the durable-mode trimmer has the same acceptance-based clock: `per_message_ttl` from `enqueued_at`, run in recovering states. So durable-mode pre-suspension inbox entries of a released interrupt session also expire on resume. EVIDENCE: spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:301, :303.
UNVERIFIED (non-spec loop): the pod release's credential release is session-wide (`Binder.releaseCredentials` → `ReleaseSession`, pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/credentiallease.go:139-144). `slotAccountLocks` orders it against a same-replica resume only. If the release outlives the REG-COORDLEASE TTL after the clear, a peer could adopt the session through a later `resume_pending` write and assign leases that the old release then revokes. SPEC-1g ("returns its leases"; "never revokes a lease that another attempt holds") states this correctly, so the issue is in the code only.

FACT: the credential trace holds in spec. The suspension release returns the old pod's leases (SPEC-1g citing §7.1 step 23 at spec/07:54). The restore runs the pre-claim check before the claim and assigns leases after the `resuming` write and before Resume. A stopped attempt releases only its own leases. A replica crash mid-attempt leaks leases until their TTL, which is the same as the finalize path, and no lease reaper exists anywhere in spec/04 §4.9, so this predates 0092.
WATCHOUT: residuals that are stranded until the next resume (a failed hold-time `resume_pending` write, or a failed or skipped release-time check) are OD-P3 territory and stated in SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.**. Do not file them as reliability findings. EVIDENCE: summary.md:111, spec-changes.md:524.
WATCHOUT: a failed release-time inbox migration loses in-memory entries even though the release is voluntary (nothing forces it the way a pod failure forces `resume_pending`). spec.2.fix-G1.2 weighed aborting and rejected it. Retrying the migration while the releasing replica lives was not weighed. Judged below the bar because the loss is stated, counted, and alerted.

The §4.6.1 **Live binding states** predicate drains a claim whose pod no session's `pod_assignment` names once `claimOrphanTimeout` passes. Credential leases left unreturned there expire by `leaseTTLSeconds`. EVIDENCE: spec/04_system-components.md:517, :1253.
WATCHOUT: The accepted release-migration window ([spec.1.fix-design-G1.1] WATCHOUT, review-log.md:939) leaks more than a sender notification. §7.3 **DLQ drain on terminal transition:** deletes the DLQ key once (spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:444). TTL expiry is enforced only in recovering states. So entries migrated after a serving-replica terminal drain (SPEC-2d item 2) stay in Redis with no reclaimer. I still did not file it, because the window is one Redis pipeline after a commit and no path widens it. Refile only with a widening path, or if a later round decides a permanent key leak is enough. The remedy is to extend SPEC-5i **Enqueue racing a terminal transition.** to the release migration (re-read; if terminal, remove the entries and emit `target_terminated`).
USEFUL [spec.1.fix-design-G1.1]: it recorded the clear-then-migrate ordering and why migrate-before-clear duplicates delivery, which settled the terminal-race question without re-deriving it.

### [spec.6.review-security.1]

FACT: Credential leases are per session on every pod, so a slot release at suspension (SPEC-5b step 2, concurrent pool) revokes only that session's leases and does not touch a sibling's. EVIDENCE: spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:26 (**Per-session credential lease lifecycle.**).
FACT: The mid-resume snapshot-close step 3 sends the pod through the pool's default post-session scrub, and step 5 runs the session-wide credential release. A podless-`suspended` terminate served off-holder (SPEC-2d item 2) that lands on a `resuming` row therefore still revokes the attempt's leases, and the attempt releases its own pod when its next write misses. The failure mode is closed. EVIDENCE: spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:220-222.
FACT: The security bounds this proposal touches are all held by trusted components. The suspended lifetime and the idle and backlog predicates read Postgres `SuspendedAt`, `SuspendedReason`, and `last_agent_activity_at`, which the gateway writes. Budget keys keep the §8.3 sentinel, so a lapsed key fails closed in the spec. Retry accounting advances on gateway-observed failure edges. None of these bounds comes from a pod self-report. EVIDENCE: spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:406-408; spec-changes.md SPEC-1b **Retry accounting.**, SPEC-5g, SPEC-5o.
USEFUL [Standing context Open "Redis DLQ and inbox keys outside §12.8 user erasure"]: it stopped a refile of the erasure-scope gap, which RECORDS-1 7(k) records with the owner's default applied.

### [non-spec-recheck.2.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: CODE-6 item 4 step 4 releases through `releaseReportedBinding(ctx, row.ID, bind, DispositionCompleted)` over the `*BindResult` the Design binding check read, skipping step 5 on a skip — BECAUSE the lock orders step 4 only against `releaseEarlierBinding`; pointer identity under the lock also orders it against `completeResume`'s publish, since a Put can only follow `releaseEarlierBinding`'s Remove of the snapshot under the same lock — ALTERNATIVES: SandboxName == PodAssignment (a same-pod slot or a re-claimed recycled pod carries the old name, so it releases the replacement); a new compare-and-release executor method (second copy of the predicate); holding the lock across steps 3 to 4 (lock held over unbounded Redis/Postgres calls, still needs identity for another replica's driver).
DECISION: `releaseReportedBinding` gains a `disposition` parameter and a `bool` result (true only when `releaseExecutor` ran and returned nil); the funnel passes `DispositionFailed` and ignores the result — BECAUSE step 4 must stop before step 5 on both a skip and an error, and the helper today returns nothing and logs its own error.
WATCHOUT: a step-4 release that runs after a concurrent resume published removes the NEW binding, because `PodExecutor.Release` keys on session ID; the row is left `running` naming a released pod and no stream-failure report follows (closedByGateway) — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/session/executor/pod.go `unbind`, `Release`; pkg/gateway/sessionserver/failure.go `releaseReportedBinding`.
CORRECTS [review-log FACT "PodExecutor.Release on an unbound session returns nil ... revokes no new leases"]: true only when step 4 runs before the attempt's publish; after the publish an unconditional release finds the replacement binding and revokes its leases. The identity test in step 4 closes it.

### [non-spec-recheck.2.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: CODE-6 item 4 step 4 releases through `releaseReportedBinding` (given a disposition parameter) with the `*BindResult` the Design binding check read, under `slotAccountLocks` — BECAUSE the existing helper already tests "registry still returns this exact *BindResult" (pkg/gateway/sessionserver/failure.go:276-284), and under the lock that test is atomic against a resume: completeResume can publish only after its releaseEarlierBinding (same lock, resume_rebind.go:168-178) has removed the snapshotted entry — ALTERNATIVES: comparing registry SandboxName with row.PodAssignment (the reviewer's suggestion) was rejected, see WATCHOUT; a new compare-and-release method on PodExecutor was rejected as a second copy of releaseReportedBinding's predicate.
WATCHOUT: a sandbox-name identity test does not discriminate. On a slot pool the resume can take a new slot on the same pod, and on a recycling exclusive pool releaseEarlierBinding returns the pod to idle and the same session's resume can re-claim it; both publish a binding whose SandboxName equals the old PodAssignment, and step 4 would release it. Pointer identity of the *BindResult is the test that discriminates — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/bindrequest.go:130-143 (SandboxName, SlotID); resume_rebind.go:124 (fresh result.Result Put).
CORRECTS [review-log FACT at ~line 1489, "PodExecutor.Release on an unbound session returns nil ... revokes no new leases"]: true only while the resume has not yet published. Once completeResume Puts the replacement binding the session is bound again and an unguarded step-4 `releaseExecutor` (keyed on session ID, executor/pod.go:202-208, :257-262) unbinds and releases the NEW binding and revokes its leases. The lock alone orders step 4 against releaseEarlierBinding, not against the later publish.
FACT: `releaseReportedBinding` has exactly one caller today (failure.go:239), so adding a disposition parameter touches one call site.
WATCHOUT: a skipped step 4 emits nothing in step 5; the pod was released by the resume's releaseEarlierBinding with DispositionFailed, not by the suspension release. SPEC-5b §6.2 step 2 prose and the SPEC-5q metric row stay true.

### [non-spec.1.review-kubernetes.1]
USEFUL [Standing context, Settled "Kubernetes surface"]: confirmed again. The proposal adds no CRD field, status write, finalizer, webhook, or request-path reconcile. Its only apiserver writes are by-name `SandboxClaim` DELETEs (CODE-3 item 3, CODE-4 items 5.3 and 20.4, CODE-6 item 4), all through the existing `podclaim.DeleteClaim`.
FACT: Deleting a claim while the pod projects `claimed` (binding state `bound`) drains and then terminates the pod. Only a claim deleted from `reserved` returns the pod to `idle`. So the CODE-3 "release after the claim" drains the freshly claimed warm pod rather than returning it to inventory. That fails closed and is not a defect. EVIDENCE: spec/04_system-components.md:414-415 (occupancy projection list).
FACT: The orphan-claim GC's "no active session references the pod" check is `GetActiveSlotsByPod`, which counts every non-terminal row whose `pod_assignment` names the pod. A held-pod `suspended` row protects its claim. A podless `suspended` row, and a replacement pod before the commit, do not. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/session/sessionstore/pgstore/pgstore.go:742-757; cmd/lenny-controller/main.go:168-185.
WATCHOUT: A by-name `DeleteClaim` (no UID or resourceVersion precondition) is ABA-safe only when the pod cannot be re-claimed under the same `claim-<pod>` name in between. Every DELETE this proposal adds runs on a claim its own attempt holds, or after a GC drain that retires the pod, so none of them can hit a successor's claim. A new late DELETE on a reserved or rebound pod would not be ABA-safe, and finalize.go records why. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/finalize.go:507-513; spec/04_system-components.md:420.

### [non-spec.1.review-performance.1]
DECISION: Filed CODE-6 item 14's `RearmTree` as a per-suspension full-keyspace SCAN — BECAUSE the spec-recheck OPEN (review-log.md:1328) explicitly deferred it to the non-spec loop and the history lists it neither fixed nor refuted; SCAN MATCH visits every key on the node, so each call costs ceil(N/256) SCAN commands for every session's entry to and exit from `suspended`, root or not; at Tier 3 (10,000 sessions, 900 s idle default, about 22 calls/s) the ~400 ops/s delegation concern (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1202) is exceeded once the node holds about 4,600 keys — ALTERNATIVES: leaving it OPEN again (rejected: no later loop owns it).
FACT: Budget keys are never deleted at tree settle in code. The reserve script arms the TTL only when TTL == -1 (treebudget.go:179-181), and the only deleter is `PurgeRoot`, whose only caller is GDPR erasure (cmd/lenny-gateway/adminrouter.go:528). Key lifetime therefore equals the TTL, which CODE-6 item 14 raises from 24 h to 691200 s. — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegationtree/treebudget/treebudget.go:38-43, :474-500
OPEN: the 8x TTL raise multiplies retained delegation-budget keys (and Redis memory on a noeviction instance) by about 8 because spec/08:1116's settle-time cleanup is unimplemented. No spec memory figure for the delegation concern was found, so this was not filed; a reviewer with a tree-creation-rate estimate should check it against the Tier 3 8 GB/node row (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1189-1193).
FACT: The lease store is wrapped in `leasestore.NewFailover` (cmd/lenny-gateway/redis_quota.go:210), so the Design lease gate keeps working through a Redis outage via the Postgres fallback. Do not refile "lease gate fails closed on Redis outage".
WATCHOUT: CODE-1 item 1's migration `ADD COLUMN ... CHECK (...)` makes Postgres scan the whole `sessions` table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE (measured: 0 ms without the CHECK, 511 ms with it, on a 3M-row temp table in lenny-postgres pg16). It also omits `IF NOT EXISTS` (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:447), but only 34 of 103 ADD COLUMN migrations in the tree use it. Neither was filed, because no spec migration-downtime bound exists.
USEFUL [review-log.md:1328 OPEN on RearmTree]: located the defect directly.
USEFUL [Standing context "Refuted: the 7-day suspended population", "Refuted: store-outage degradation"]: settled the Sweeper Get, HeldLen, and Redis-outage DLQ candidates without re-deriving them.

### [non-spec.1.review-security.1]
DECISION: filed one finding: the client-driven `awaiting_client_action` -> `/resume` -> `resume_pending` -> `awaiting_client_action` cycle lets a root stay outside `suspended` past the 8 d budget-key TTL, and in code an expired key reads as 0, so the tree budget silently resets. BECAUSE today `sweepMaxAge` expires every non-terminal row at wall-clock age from `CreatedAt` (2 h default), so the TTL is unreachable at defaults, and CODE-1 removes that cap for the recovery states while CODE-6 item 14 re-arms only on `suspended` entry and exit. ### [non-spec.2.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: CODE-4 item 23's renewal stop moves from a replica-local release observer to the shared lease store. `Renew` refuses (ErrLeaseReleased) when `w.leases.GetByID(spent)` has no record or the spent lease has no pool binding, re-reads the spent lease after `Assign` and releases the replacement when it is gone, and both `ReleaseSession` implementations list the session's leases a second time after their removals. `Assigner.OnReleased`, `credRenewalWiring.forget`, and the `Forget` doc-comment rewrite are deleted — BECAUSE the observer fires only on the releasing replica (finding 2) and its timing against `OnAssigned`/the post-check is unordered (findings 0, 1); the store is what every replica's release writes. The two writes form a Dekker pair (Renew: Put replacement, then read spent; release: remove spent, then re-list), so every interleaving is caught by one side. One re-list suffices: a replacement Put after the spent removal is caught by Renew's post-check. — ALTERNATIVES: forget(replacement) inside Renew (finding 0's fix; still replica-local, misses finding 1 and 2); successor map spent→replacement in w.pools (replica-local, new state); firing OnReleased before store removal (still replica-local); a loop-until-empty re-list (unbounded; one re-list is provably enough).
FACT: The renewal wiring's `w.leases` is the same `llmLeases` store both assigners Put into and Remove from (Service via `credassign.New(llmLeases, ...)`, Client via `ClientOptions.Leases`), Postgres-backed whenever pgPool is set. — EVIDENCE: cmd/lenny-gateway/executor_credentials.go:71-86,133-146; cmd/lenny-gateway/revocation.go:86
FACT: Both `OnAssigned` observers (Service and Client) run synchronously before `Assign` returns, so by the time `Renew`'s post-check runs the replacement is already tracked; a released-but-tracked replacement is dropped by the store pre-check at its own RenewBefore, so no `Forget` call is needed. — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/credentials/credassign/credassign.go:268-278; client.go:164-171
WATCHOUT: Five renewal tests in cmd/lenny-gateway/cred_renewal_test.go (lines ~105, 163, 222, 279, 322) and two in cred_renewal_extend_wiring_test.go (~365, 435) build the wiring with a nil lease store and expect a mint. Under the store check (nil counts as no record, fail closed) they must pass a store holding the renewed lease. Do not make a nil store skip the check: that is the leak.
WATCHOUT: In the no-Postgres mode the lease store is per-replica in-memory, so the cross-replica stop does not hold there; that mode does not resolve leases across replicas at all. — EVIDENCE: executor_credentials.go:67-71
OPEN (separate finding, not staged): a by-ID release (`releaseAttemptCredentials` in ReleaseUncommitted/failResume, Token Service `Release`) of a lease whose renewal already passed its post-check leaves the replacement live and renewing; neither the old observer design nor the store design catches it, because the release names only the spent ID. Requires leaseTTL - renewBeforeBuffer shorter than the attempt; reachable with a small `leaseTTLSeconds`.
CORRECTS [review-log 1834, 1836, 1837, 1866, 1869, 1899]: the `OnReleased` observer, its after-unlock WATCHOUTs, and "cross-replica is the same residual class" are superseded; the stop now reads the shared lease store and the cross-replica case is closed, not residual.
CORRECTS [review-log 1835]: "self-healing because the next Renew finds no pool binding" — the binding is replica-local and is moved to the replacement by a successful Renew; self-healing now comes from the store pre-check.

### [non-spec.2.follow-up-fix.1]
DECISION: CODE-4 item 23 keeps the shared-store release test and makes absence authoritative: a new `LeaseStore.Lookup(leaseID) (Lease, bool, error)` (pgstore: not-found only on `pgx.ErrNoRows`; scan, KMS, and decode failures are errors that `Renew` returns as ordinary retryable failures), and new sub-item 4: `onExtend` advances the row's `ExpiresAt`/`RenewBefore` on both delivery modes through a new update-only `LeaseStore.Advance(lease) (bool, error)`, direct branch before the RPC; `Advance` finding no row returns `ErrLeaseReleased`, which `Tick` drops as sub-item 3 states. A post-`Assign` lookup error releases the replacement, deletes only its pool binding, and returns the error. BECAUSE the direct branch never wrote the row, so the sweep removed an extended live lease's row and `Renew` read that as a release; and `scanLease` folds every failure into ok=false. ALTERNATIVES: skip the pre-Assign read for extended leases (the post-Assign read still misreads the swept row once the breaker closes); advance via `Put` (an upsert that resurrects a lease a concurrent release removed between `GetByID` and `Put`, which defeats item 23 and, for proxy rows, re-validates a released token); change `GetByID`'s signature (dozens of callers).
FACT: Shipped `onExtend` already fails a direct-mode lease's second extension once the sweep removed its row (`GetByID` miss -> error -> recordFailure -> exhaust into the Fallback Flow), so the §4.9 cap teardown was effectively unreachable in direct mode; item 23 sub-item 4 fixes that as a side effect. EVIDENCE: cmd/lenny-gateway/cred_renewal.go `onExtend` (GetByID before the delivery-mode switch); credential_lease_sweep.go `sweepExpiredCredentialLeases`; pgstore.go DeleteExpired `expires_at < $1`.
WATCHOUT: The shipped proxy branch of `onExtend` is a `GetByID` then `Put` upsert and can resurrect a row a concurrent release removed; sub-item 4's `Advance` replaces it. Do not "simplify" `Advance` back to `Put`. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/credentials/credleasestore/pgstore/pgstore.go `Put` (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE).
WATCHOUT: With the row tracking the worker's `ExpiresAt`, a sweep can remove a live row only under cross-replica clock skew larger than the renew-before buffer, because `Tick` exhausts any lease past its tracked `ExpiresAt` before calling `Renew`. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/credentials/credrenewal/credrenewal.go `Tick` expiresAt guard.
CORRECTS [review-log DECISION lines 1834 and 1866, ALTERNATIVES "lease-store existence check"]: the objection (pgstore `GetByID` reads a DB error as not-found) is now answered by `Lookup`'s error return, not by avoiding the store read.
FACT: Citer sweep over "item 23", `ErrLeaseReleased`, `GetByID`, `Lookup`, `Advance`, and "renewal stop" across all proposal files: the checklist S12 and summary CODE-4 rows only name "the renewal stop for a released lease" and stay true; no other site describes sub-items 2-4. spec-changes.md untouched.

### [non-spec.8.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: the re-route after `sessionidle.ErrSessionSuspended` (CODE-6 item 7) re-reads the row on the primary as `holdMessage` does (CODE-4 item 7), and the first message-path re-read stays a `store.Get` — BECAUSE the first stale replica read is caught by the `StampSync` primary admission, while a re-route that re-reads the replica reclassifies `running` and loops until the replica catches up — ALTERNATIVES: every re-read on the primary (wider than the defect); a retry bound or backoff (a second mechanism that still classifies a stale row).
WATCHOUT: the re-route's discriminating test needs a store whose `Get` returns `running` after the row is `suspended`; memstore has no lag, so a plain memstore run passes on the old text. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md Tests entry `TestHeldMessagesDeliveredBeforeNewMessage`.
FACT: the MCP path's `deps.Store` is the full `sessionstore.Store`, so it can run the `Update` primary re-read; `errHoldReread` is a `sessionserver` package sentinel, so the MCP package needs its own no-write sentinel or reaches the read through `SessionDelivery`. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/mcptools.go:351

### [non-spec.8.review-mechanism.1]
DECISION: filed one finding: the ErrSessionSuspended re-route in CODE-6 items 5.4 and 7 reclassifies a row the message path reads through store.Get, which is the read replica, so when the replica lags behind SuspendIdle's commit the path keeps classifying `running`, and StampSync keeps refusing on the primary. The loop has no bound, no backoff, and no primary read. BECAUSE: the same replica-staleness defect was already fixed for holdMessage's re-read (errHoldReread), and StampSync has just read the row on the primary as `suspended`. ALTERNATIVES: filing it as performance-only (rejected because the loop has no termination condition other than replica catch-up).
FACT: pgstore.Get, List, and ListByRoot read `s.read`, which is the --pg-read-dsn pool when that flag is set and the primary otherwise. Every "re-read the row" in the message paths, ResumeSuspended, DeliverHeld, and handleResume is a replica read unless the text says primary. FACT: §29.3 rows for a podless suspended session all have a server once SPEC-2d, SPEC-3j, and SPEC-5l land. Messages and resume use a store write on any replica. Terminate and delete go through handleTransition (store write) and recordSessionCompleted, which drains the DLQ; Checkpointer.Seal returns nil when the replica holds no binding. Resolution goes through resolveInteraction (interaction store). Events JSON is served from SubscribeForTenant's backlog, which merges the relay. Interrupt and upload do not admit `suspended`. ### [redesign5.apply.1]

DECISION: Redesign 5 (2026-10-09) was applied from `scratchpad/redesign/0092_new_write-the-session-suspend-and-resume-proposal-that-gateway-redesign-1.md`. Every edit it lists applied, 1 to 77 with 39a and the lettered parts; each anchor resolved exactly once, and no edit was skipped. It redesigned five areas: session-row read authority (rules R1 to R3, the non-spec Design paragraph **Session-row read authority.**, `sessionstore.ReadPrimary`, and the sentinels `errMaxAgeSuperseded`, `errResumePendingSuperseded`, `errOrphanSuperseded`, `errStampSkipped`, and `errIdleSuspendSuperseded`, plus the `RecordHandoff` locked-row `adoptedState` check); OD-P3 as a gateway-leader backlog re-check of podless `suspended` sessions (SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.**, SPEC-5n, SPEC-5s, CODE-6 item 16, migration 0183); OD-C1 as no new mechanism (Decision 23 as staged); OD-C2 as a §12.8 user-erasure step for the session DLQ and durable inbox (SPEC-5aa, Decision 24, CODE-6 item 17); and OD-C3 as a generation-scoped pod-release lease return (SPEC-1g, SPEC-1f item 3, new SPEC-1g3 renewal-loop step 1, CODE-4 item 24). BECAUSE: the tree's `pgstore.Get`, `GetByID`, `List`, and `ListByRoot` read the §12.3 read pool, which produced four verified defects (duplicate sweep side effects, the lost `ReportSessionFailure` report, `RecordHandoff` re-adopting a failed pod, and the unspecified re-reads of `ResumeSuspended` and `DeliverHeld`), and the four open decisions were resolved on 2026-10-09 under the owner's delegation.
DECISION: Deleted by the redesign: the summary's open-decision entries OD-P3, OD-C1, OD-C2, and OD-C3 with both preambles; the Non-goals bullet that excluded a periodic backlog evaluation on the gateway leader; the Defects bullet **Redis session DLQ and inbox outside user erasure.**; RECORDS-1 item 7(k) as the erasure finding (its letter now files the nil-returning watchdog mutators); the accepted residual that a pod release on a replica that lost the lease revokes a peer restore's leases (SPEC-1f item 3 and both Edge-cases rows); the sentinel `errHoldReread`; the lease-ordering rationale of the CODE-4 item 22 lock (its lead, its field-comment bullet, the summary watch-out, and CODE-6 item 4 step 4); and the summary's replica-read watch-out.
DECISION: Reconciliation beyond the redesign's own edits: CODE-6 item 7's lead now reads the row with `sessionstore.ReadPrimary`; the TEST-1 tier-7a test `TestSuspensionReleaseRacingResumeKeepsNewLeases` uses a lease store that records `CoordinationGeneration`, and its diagnosis names the binding tear-down as well as the lease revocation; the summary Defects list gains the nil-returning watchdog mutators (RECORDS-1 item 7(k)) and the missing tenant-deletion queue erasure (RECORDS-1 item 7(p)). The checklist dependencies needed no change: S13 already depends on S5 (SPEC-5aa) and S12 (`ReadPrimary`, `enterResumePending`), and S10 uses no `ReadPrimary`.
DECISION: The CODE-4 item 22 `slotAccountLocks` lock stays with a narrower rationale. BECAUSE: `releaseReportedBinding` checks the binding by pointer identity and then releases by session ID (failure.go:276-288), so without the lock a same-replica driver attempt can publish a replacement binding that the funnel's `releaseExecutor` then tears down. EVIDENCE: redesign section 2, conflict 3.
FACT: No open decision remains after this redesign. The redesign's section 4 lists the candidates it considered (fixing rather than filing the remaining nil-returning watchdog mutators, deleting the item 22 lock, and the attribution wording) and applied a default to each.
CORRECTS [Standing context Trap "Replaced: the unlocked suspension and funnel releases."]: the lock no longer protects a resume's new leases; CODE-4 item 24's generation scope does. The lock keeps the replacement binding from the funnel's and the suspension release's `releaseExecutor`.
CORRECTS [Standing context OPEN "the Redis DLQ and inbox keys outside §12.8 user erasure are filed as RECORDS-1 item 7(k)"]: closed. SPEC-5aa and CODE-6 item 17 stage the erasure, and item 7(k) now files the nil-returning watchdog mutators.
CORRECTS [mechanism.podless-session-coordination.1 WATCHOUT "Do not restore a periodic `HeldLen` probe on podless rows"] and [redesign2.apply.1 WATCHOUT on the periodic backlog evaluation]: the per-replica probe stays deleted, and the gateway leader now re-checks podless rows (CODE-6 item 16). SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.** states no residual.
CORRECTS [redesign2.apply.1 WATCHOUT "Replaced: migration 0183 with `ListFilter.SuspendedAtOrBefore`"]: migration 0183 is now the podless partial index `idx_sessions_podless_suspended` that the leader re-check reads. The listing filters stay deleted, and RECORDS-1 item 7(l) still files the other listings.
WATCHOUT: Replaced: the per-site `errHoldReread` primary re-read in `holdMessage`. Each site carried its own sentinel and prose, and the other one-shot reads (`handleResume`, `attemptResume`, `ReportSessionFailure`, `ReportAttachStreamFailure`, `persistDeriveFailure`, `ResumeSuspended`, and `DeliverHeld`) read the replica. `sessionstore.ReadPrimary` is the one primary read; do not reintroduce a per-site sentinel or a `store.Get` read that decides a write.
WATCHOUT: Replaced: nil-returning `Update` mutators that decide not to write in `sweepResumePending`, `sweepMaxAge`, `failOrphan`, `StampSync`, and `SuspendIdle`. A nil return writes the row, advances `UpdatedAt`, and lets a second replica repeat the side effects. Each now returns a sentinel; do not return nil from a mutator that declines to write.
WATCHOUT: Replaced: the accepted residual that a pod release on a replica that lost the lease revokes a peer restore's credential leases (former OD-C3 default). It lost because the generation stamp is already on the binding and the lease record is sealed JSON, so scoping needs no migration. Do not return a session-wide `ReleaseSession` from `Release` or `ReleaseSlot`; only `failPhase`, `ReclaimClaimed`, and `revokeFinalizeLease` keep it.
WATCHOUT: Replaced: the accepted residual of held messages stranded on a podless `suspended` session until its next resume or its lifetime (former OD-P3 default). It lost to a coarse gateway-leader re-check over a partial index. Do not move that evaluation back onto every replica's watchdog tick.
WATCHOUT: Do not add a separate SPEC-2a sentence that names the leader's evaluation as the only periodic work on a podless session; the Sweeper and the watchdog lifetime check also read such rows, and SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.** is the one statement.

The sentence moved after the failed-delivery consequences — BECAUSE placed before "The path-2 message ... handled as if its own delivery had failed" it read as that sentence's trigger, stalling every session on a Redis outage; CODE-4 item 6 (nil on a Peek/PeekOldest error) already matches — ALTERNATIVES: path-2-only clause in place (leaves the synchronous outcome unstated and the misleading order).

### [spec.1.fix-G2.1]
DECISION: A held-message read failure (inbox `Peek` or DLQ `PeekOldest`) is not a failed delivery. SPEC-5i **Delivery of held messages.** now says so in one sentence, and CODE-4 item 6 has `deliverBuffered` log it at WARN and return nil. BECAUSE: a returned Peek error would fail every path-2 Send during a session-data Redis outage, which stalls every running session and conflicts with §12.4's rule that existing sessions keep running. Returning nil leaves CODE-6 item 7's "handled as an error of that `executor.Send`" rule correct for every caller. ALTERNATIVES: an `errHeldReadFailed` sentinel with a branch at each caller, rejected because it adds a type for no different outcome; the reviewer's wording naming path 2 only, rejected because it is narrower and longer.
WATCHOUT: A removal (`LREM`/`ZREM`) error is not a read failure. The runtime has already consumed the entry, so it stays a returned error. Do not fold it into the nil-return case. — EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-4 item 6, server-lifetime-context bullet
CORRECTS [Standing context "Refuted: store-outage degradation"]: that entry refutes Redis-outage DLQ-peek findings only as message loss. The availability stall (every path-2 Send failing through the peek) was a confirmed finding in spec.1 of redesign 6, and the spec now closes it. Do not use that entry to refute the stall case.

### [spec.1.fix-design-G2.1]
DECISION: an inbox or DLQ read failure in **Delivery of held messages.** (SPEC-5i) is not a failed delivery; the replica stops delivering held messages and the unread entries wait for the next delivery point, so path 2 and synchronous delivery proceed — BECAUSE the DLQ is always Redis, and treating a read error as a failed delivery routes every path-2 message to the inbox during a session-data Redis outage, worse than shipped path 2 — ALTERNATIVES: a distinct error sentinel that CODE-6 item 7 branches on (adds a type and a branch at every caller for one outcome; returning nil is the same behavior with no new surface); keeping the stall (contradicts the storage-section posture that existing sessions keep running through a Redis outage).
WATCHOUT: the code home is CODE-4 item 6 alone: a `Peek`/`PeekOldest` error logs WARN and returns nil. CODE-6 item 7 ("handles its error as an error of that `executor.Send`") stays true and must NOT gain a read-error branch. `Send` and removal errors still return the error. — EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-4 item 6 ctx bullet; CODE-6 item 7 lead.
WATCHOUT: under a read failure a path-2 or synchronous message reaches the runtime ahead of older held entries; this ordering loss is the accepted cost of the decision above, and the new spec sentence is what licenses it. A reviewer filing "oldest-first violated" should be pointed here.

### [spec.1.review-mechanism.1]

FACT: The `lenny-gateway-leader` Lease that SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.** cites is defined in §12.5 (artifact GC, "gateway-scoped singleton jobs use an equivalent `lenny-gateway-leader` Lease"), with a failover window of up to 25 s on a crash, and the code already has it. FACT: §4.9 renewal is a per-replica min-heap (`CredentialRenewalWorker`). SPEC-1g3 changes only step 1. A takeover leaves the old replica's heap renewing un-released leases, and that behavior predates 0092. EVIDENCE: spec/04_system-components.md:1541-1543.
FACT: Under SPEC-1g, a pod release never returns a later restore's leases. Every restore's entry write increments `coordination_generation`, and so does every takeover. Leases from finalize and other non-restore assignments record 0, so they are always at or below any binding stamp. I traced a release racing a peer's restore (the suspension release on A, then a takeover on B, then a restore at G+2) and a same-replica restore while A still holds the unexpired lease. Both hold. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md SPEC-1g; SPEC-1f item 2.
WATCHOUT: SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.** says "No replica other than the gateway leader evaluates such a session periodically." Read literally, that bars the per-replica watchdog's lifetime expiry of podless `suspended` rows (non-spec CODE-6 item 2 sub-item 1 runs before the podless skip) and the SPEC-5d expiry. Scope the sentence to the backlog condition. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md:528; non-spec-changes.md:194-196.
WATCHOUT: In SPEC-1g, the lead sentence "Each credential lease records the session's `coordination_generation` at its assignment" contradicts the two sentences after it: a non-restore lease records 0, and a renewal or rotation records the generation of the lease it replaces. Non-spec item 24 leaves finalize, create, start, and child at 0. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md:157; non-spec-changes.md:168.

### [spec.2.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: The gateway leader evaluates the podless backlog condition at once on Lease acquisition (SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.** last sentence; CODE-6 item 16.3 `Run` calls `Pass` once, then ticks) — BECAUSE `gatewayleader.Gate.Run` relaunches every job fresh on each acquisition with no schedule carried across leaders, so a ticker-only `Run` makes the delay interval plus failover and leadership churn under a rolling update starves the pass — ALTERNATIVES: restating the bound as interval plus failover window (churn still starves it); persisting a last-pass timestamp (new shared state and write paths).
FACT: Leader-gated jobs start fresh on every Lease acquisition via `go job.Run(leaderCtx)` inside the onStarted callback. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/coordination/gatewayleader/gatewayleader.go:221-228
WATCHOUT: The immediate-pass pin lives in session-server `TestBacklogRecheckerResumesPodlessHeld_spec_7_2` (it holds the fake clock); cmd `TestSuspendedBacklogRecheckLeaderGated` covers only gating and registration. Do not move it. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md test list
USEFUL [FACT review-log:2446 lenny-gateway-leader 25 s failover bound in §12.5]: confirmed the bound the new sentence relies on. EVIDENCE: spec/12_storage-architecture.md:358

### [spec.2.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: Close the leader-failover bound on the podless backlog re-check by having the job evaluate when it acquires the Lease. In the SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.** last sentence, CODE-6 item 16.3 `Run` changes to Pass first and then the ticker, and one assertion goes in the session-server Run/Pass test. BECAUSE `gatewayleader.Gate.Run` relaunches every job fresh on each acquisition, so a ticker-only Run delays the first pass by a full interval after failover, and repeated leadership moves less than one interval apart starve it. ALTERNATIVES: (a) restating the bound as "interval plus failover window" still leaves leadership churn starving the pass; (b) persisting the last-pass time across leaders adds new state that nothing else needs.
FACT: `Gate.Run` launches `go job.Run(leaderCtx)` for every job inside the onStarted callback on each acquisition, and no schedule carries over between leaders. A leader-gated job therefore gets an immediate evaluation on failover only when its own Run passes before its first tick. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/coordination/gatewayleader/gatewayleader.go:221-228
FACT: The crash failover window of the `lenny-gateway-leader` Lease is "up to 25s on crash". EVIDENCE: spec/12_storage-architecture.md:358
WATCHOUT: The test that discriminates is that `Run` calls `Pass` before the fake clock advances. The cmd-level `TestSuspendedBacklogRecheckLeaderGated` tests only gating and registration, so the immediate-pass assertion belongs to the session-server test that holds the clock.

### [spec.2.review-performance.1]
DECISION: filed one finding: SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.** "A leader failover delays that evaluation by at most the Lease failover window" has no mechanism behind it. `gatewayleader.Gate.Run` launches each job on acquisition and CODE-6 item 16.3 runs `Pass` on a ticker, so the new leader's first pass comes one full interval after it acquires the Lease. The real bound is the interval plus 25 s, and a gateway rolling update that moves leadership faster than every 300 s starves the re-check. Remedy: state in the spec that a replica that acquires the Lease evaluates at once (code: `Pass` before the ticker). BECAUSE the bound is a failure-mode guarantee the spec states and the staged code cannot meet. ALTERNATIVES: deleting the sentence (rejected: the edge case "bounds it by the gateway leader's re-check interval" stays false under failover).
FACT: Gate.Run starts every registered job in a goroutine on each leadership acquisition, with no shared schedule across leaders. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/coordination/gatewayleader/gatewayleader.go:222-228
FACT: The largest GA tier is Tier 3 (Tier 4 is not a GA deliverable). Its figures: 200/s creation, 10,000 concurrent sessions, about 30 ends/s by Little's law, and a Redis write budget of about 6,500/s sustained. EVIDENCE: spec/16_observability.md:595-603,616; spec/12_storage-architecture.md:268-270
DECISION: did not refile the leader re-check population cost, the per-path-2 DLQ peek, the idle-suspension checkpoint and pod churn, or the release-time inbox migration loss. BECAUSE each one depends on an idle-suspension fraction the spec does not state, or is no worse than the shipped design. USEFUL [spec.1.review-performance.1]: its f-fraction DECISION and the migration-loss DECISION held on re-derivation.
WATCHOUT: spec/12_storage-architecture.md:210 calls Redis "ephemeral" with a durable fallback for every role. The DLQ and durable inbox have no row in the failure-behavior table at all. This gap predates 0092 (the recovering-state DLQ was already Redis-only), so do not file it against 0092 unless a loss case is new.

### [spec.2.review-security.1]
DECISION: no security finding in the spec staging this round — BECAUSE the round-1 fixes (SPEC-1g lead sentence, leader-only backlog sentence, held-delivery read-failure sentence, SPEC-5z item 4 deletion) touch no control, and the SPEC-1g generation rule holds on every trace tried — ALTERNATIVES: filing the SPEC-2d item 2 podless terminate as an unconditioned write (rejected: below the bar, see UNVERIFIED).
FACT: SPEC-1g lease return traced across suspension release, stale-replica release, same-replica release racing its own restore (the lease is still held in resume_pending, so no takeover CAS runs, but the resuming write still increments), and crashed-attempt leases. Every restore's leases carry a generation above every earlier binding stamp, so no release returns them. Leases a crashed attempt minted are returned by the next binding's release or revoked at terminal (§6.1), and the lease TTL bounds them otherwise — EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md:157, spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:26.
FACT: on recycling pools, a suspension release advances the served-session count through the Shutdown's ReportSessionScrub like any session release, so maxSessionsPerPod still bounds reuse — EVIDENCE: spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md:462.
UNVERIFIED: SPEC-2d item 2 lets the serving replica terminate a podless `suspended` session itself. The staged text does not condition the terminal write on the row still being podless `suspended`, so a restore that commits `running` between the read and the write could be terminated without the coordinator's pod sequence. The window is one full restore. The orphan-claim GC bounds the pod. Whoever owns read authority or terminal writes should check whether the code's terminal mutator re-checks the state.
UNVERIFIED: SPEC-2d item 3 "records the resolution" for a podless `suspended` session. toolapproval's ErrNotFound path still updates the interaction phase (pkg/gateway/session/toolapproval/toolapproval.go:27-30). Nobody has checked whether a restored runtime that re-emits the same toolCallId could pick up a recorded approval.

### [spec.3.review-performance.1]
DECISION: no findings under the performance and failure-mode lens in spec round 3 — BECAUSE the only spec change since round 2 (SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.**: "A replica that acquires the Lease evaluates the condition at once") gives the failover bound a mechanism, and the leader re-check's cost is bounded by the concurrency caps — ALTERNATIVES: filing the leader re-check as a single-leader O(population) bottleneck; rejected by the math below.
FACT: The podless `suspended` population is bounded by the concurrent-session admission caps, because every non-terminal row counts toward them (spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:1111; review-log [spec.6.review-performance.1]). At the Tier 4 ceiling of 100,000 concurrent sessions (spec/16_observability.md:595), one leader pass is at most 100,000 rows × 1–2 Redis reads (ZCARD/ZCOUNT plus LLEN for `Idle`) every 300 s, which is about 333–667 ops/s. Sequentially at ~0.5 ms per read, the pass takes about 50–100 s, which is under the 300 s interval. At Tier 3 the load is about a tenth of that. The Redis budget is ~100K ops/s (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1191). Do not file the re-check as a bottleneck unless the caps stop counting suspended rows.
FACT: The "Lease failover window" that SPEC-5i cites is §12.5's "near-zero on clean shutdown; up to 25s on crash" for `lenny-gateway-leader` (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:358). The bound holds because of the new evaluate-on-acquire sentence.
WATCHOUT: The etcd estimate in §4.6.1 assumes that "on a pool without recycling the occupancy episode and the session coincide" (spec/04_system-components.md:475). An idle suspension with a hold of zero, followed by a resume, adds one claim lifecycle per idle cycle. I did not file it. Pod-failure resumes and interrupt-hold releases already broke the assumption before 0092, and the Tier 3 mean session lifetime implied by Little's law (10,000 / 30–200 per s) is well under the 900 s idle bound. Refile only with a workload figure from the spec that makes idle-resume cycles material.
OPEN (human): Abandoned podless `suspended` sessions hold a concurrent-session cap slot for up to 7 days rather than ~2 h (see [spec.6.review-performance.1] FACT). At the Tier 3 creation rate of 200/s, the 10,000 cap fills once more than about 1 in 12,000 sessions is abandoned without a terminate. Under the old 7200 s idle-terminate the threshold was about 1 in 144. This is a consequence of the plan's 7-day lifetime combined with pre-existing quota counting. I did not file it, because the remedy is a design choice (exempting podless `suspended` from the caps, or a shorter lifetime). The owner should confirm the trade-off.
USEFUL [Traps "Refuted: the 7-day suspended population"]: it scoped the HeldLen refiling rule. The leader re-check is now such a code path, so I checked its cost against the caps rather than against the 7-day population.

### [spec.4.review-reliability.1]
DECISION: returned no reliability findings on the round-4 spec staging — BECAUSE the only spec delta (SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.** "A replica that acquires the Lease evaluates the condition at once") closes the failover-starvation gap: the delay past the scheduled evaluation is bounded by the §12.5 failover window (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:358, up to 25 s on crash), and churn cannot starve it because every acquisition evaluates. The whole-staging trace also holds. Lease race: a lapsed driver whose entry write lands before the acquirer's CAS makes that CAS hit 0 rows, the acquirer discards the lease (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:37), and step 0 then finds `resuming`, which no replica adopts. Credential race: a stale release returns leases at or below its bind generation, and every restore's entry write advances past it. Release crash windows: the orphan claim goes to the claim GC, leaked leases expire on their TTL, and a missed backlog check falls to the leader re-check — ALTERNATIVES: filing the SPEC-5o re-arm loss under a Redis failure at entry to `suspended` (rejected: it needs a failed re-arm plus more than 1 day outside `suspended`, it fails closed, and RearmTree best-effort is settled); filing the 7-day Redis-only DLQ for `suspended` with no `session_dlq_archive` backing (rejected: a durability preference that contradicts no stated invariant).
WATCHOUT: §6.2 release step 3 (unchanged) lists the exits from a failed-checkpoint hold as "(cancel, terminate, `perChildMaxAge` expiry)". This list was already non-exhaustive before 0092 (resume exits too), so the new lifetime expiry does not falsify it. Do not file it. EVIDENCE: spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:230
WATCHOUT: The §7.2 "Inbox drain on terminal transition" 60 s post-mortem DLQ TTL is unenforced under SPEC-5i's "enforces it only while ... recovering" sentence. The code (`DrainOnTerminal`) drains the inbox and the DLQ together and deletes the key, so no entry persists. The spec's ordering of the two terminal drains was ambiguous before 0092. EVIDENCE: spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:352, spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:444, pkg/gateway/session/sessioninbox/coordinator.go:196-213
USEFUL [review-log FACT ~2501]: it stopped a refile of the primary-read requirement for the SPEC-5i terminal re-read, which §12.3 **Read replicas:** would otherwise make look like a spec defect.

### [non-spec.1.review-performance.1]
DECISION: Returned no findings in non-spec round 1 (redesign 6). BECAUSE the round's diff (BacklogRechecker `Run` passes once at start, SPEC-5i "A replica that acquires the Lease evaluates the condition at once", OD-S1, RECORDS lines) adds no write class; the leader re-check costs one indexed list per tenant plus one `HeldLen` per podless row per 300 s, and the podless population is bounded by the non-terminal concurrent-session caps (OD-S1, pgstore.go:864-866), so about 10,000 rows (~33 Redis ops/s) at Tier 3. `RearmTree` issues no SCAN (CODE-6 item 14 bullet 1). ALTERNATIVES: filing the per-message `ReadPrimary` (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the primary) as Postgres load; rejected because the spec states no message rate to quantify it against the §12.3 ~1,300/s sustained / ~1,600/s ceiling budget.
FACT: The leader failover bound holds with the start-time pass: `Gate.Run` launches each job on every leadership acquisition (pkg/gateway/coordination/gatewayleader/gatewayleader.go:222-229), so the delay past the scheduled pass is at most the failover window. EVIDENCE: that file.
WATCHOUT: `credleasestore` pgstore `LeasesBySession` swallows a query error and returns nil (pkg/gateway/credentials/credleasestore/pgstore/pgstore.go:216-226), so `ReleaseThrough` and `ReleaseSession` silently release nothing during a Postgres failover, and the lease keeps renewing. I weighed it below the bar: the shipped design held every lease through a suspension, and session-end release catches the leftover. Refile only with a pool-exhaustion case. EVIDENCE: that file.
